### 1.  Coordinates of the vertices  

At \(A\) the interior angle is \(90^{\circ}\); turning right \(90^{\circ}\) from side \(EA\) (which points west) makes side \(AB\) vertical upward.  
Hence  

\[
B=(0,AB).
\]

At \(B\) the interior angle is \(45^{\circ}\); turning right \(135^{\circ}\) from the upward direction gives side \(BC\) at an angle of \(-45^{\circ}\).  
Since \(BC=14\sqrt2\),

\[
C=B+(14,-14)=(14,\,AB-14).
\]

At \(C\) the interior angle is \(270^{\circ}\); this is a left turn of \(90^{\circ}\), so side \(CD\) makes a \(+45^{\circ}\) angle.  
The length \(CD\) is forced to be \(6\sqrt2\) (the only value that makes the \(x\)-coordinate of \(D\) equal to \(20\); see below). Thus

\[
D=C+(6,6)=(20,\,AB-8).
\]

Finally, at \(D\) a right turn of \(135^{\circ}\) makes side \(DE\) vertical downward, landing at  

\[
E=(20,0).
\]

Consequently  

\[
DE = AB-8.
\]

Because \(B,C,D\) must lie on the same side of line \(AE\) (the \(x\)-axis), we need \(AB>14\); then all three points are above the axis (the reflected picture below the axis gives the same conditions).

### 2.  Area of the pentagon  

Using the shoelace formula for the ordered vertices  

\[
A(0,0),\; B(0,AB),\; C(14,AB-14),\; D(20,AB-8),\; E(20,0),
\]

\[
